well feats as features.  so you might lose your lucky feat, but gain flight from being an uru, or defying death from jackalope.

a player might lose a feat, but resistance to cold, advantage on all saving throws involving cold, water breathing, etc.... casue now they are mostly chinn.

Much like the being damned, it becomes a roleplay opportunity, and then they have the ability to quest for their orriginal build.

but this is why im making two methods of coming back in hampstead.  One you keep your orriginal race, but become more damned.... i have been toying with the idea that if you are already damned, there will be other things you have to deal with.  The other will be being stiched togeather, into a new body (Frankenstein is one of the most classic of gothic horror stories).  the new body will have a chance of being the same as your old one, or at least enough the same you for it to not matter.... or you get a new race via reincarnation. (going to cannibalize some AD&D ideas on how to decide, but something akin to old system shock, where passing the check means you keep your old body, failing, and you get a new one).

Both paths will have other costs linked to them.  The Frank route will entail the players having to work the debt off by supplying parts, and getting labeled freak and monster, having to return over and over to get a new supply of blood (possibly even making it where healing is halved for a week, and resting doesnt heal, instead having to get infusions, until the person's body becomes their own once again)

The other route will cost if you need an NPC to cast the spell, especially if your soul has no body to be directly reattached to.  It might cost you faith in a new path, it might cost you penance.  I have an NPC that can cast high level rez spells (that don't necessarily need bodies to cast), but you may have to follow his more peaceful and tranquil path for him to do it.

This way players can basically pick their path, but all Hampstead paths lead to changes that should give roleplay opportunity.  Likewise those players could have their bodies or souls taken to other burroughs and deal with those mechanics
